title: EPCOT World Tour
intro: [excited] Passports out, everybody! Tonight we're strolling all the way around World Showcase, and no, you cannot stop for a churro between every clue. Let's see who's a globe-trotter and who's just lost in Canada.

art.prompt: A glittering geodesic silver sphere rising above a lagoon at twilight, ringed by a fantasy skyline of world landmarks: a Mayan-style pyramid, a pagoda, a Bavarian clock tower, a Moroccan minaret, and a miniature Eiffel-style tower, fireworks and string lights reflecting on the water Original illustration, 16:9, rich saturated colors, cinematic lighting, no people, no characters, no text, no logos.

categories.title: Little Chef, Big Paris
categories.intro: We start in France with a film about a rat who can cook. [mischievously] If you can't answer these, I'm sending you to the kitchen to peel potatoes.

art.prompt: A cozy Parisian rooftop at night overlooking a glowing city of zinc roofs and chimneys, a tiny copper saucepan of bubbling soup and a sprig of fresh herbs on the ledge, a big round moon Original illustration, 16:9, rich saturated colors, cinematic lighting, no people, no characters, no text, no logos.

clues.clue: In Ratatouille, Remy the rat dreams of becoming one of these.
clues.reveal: [cheerful] The correct answer is a chef! And in EPCOT's France pavilion, you can shrink down to Remy size on Remy's Ratatouille Adventure. Hairnets not included.

clues.clue: The famous Paris restaurant founded by Chef Auguste Gusteau.
clues.reveal: [chuckles] The correct answer is Gusteau's! Five stars, then four, then a very grumpy review. [whispers] Restaurants are tough, folks.

clues.clue: Gusteau's famous motto, which is also the title of his cookbook.
clues.reveal: [playfully] The correct answer is Anyone Can Cook! Which is true, unless you're me with a microwave burrito. [laughs] Then it's anyone can burn.

clues.clue: Peter O'Toole voiced this terrifying food critic who writes in a coffin-shaped office.
clues.reveal: [impressed] The correct answer is Anton Ego! One bite of Remy's ratatouille sent him straight back to his mom's kitchen. That's the power of comfort food.

clues.clue: Remy's fancy layered ratatouille was inspired by this dish, a version made for the film's consultant, chef Thomas Keller.
clues.reveal: [whispers] The correct answer is confit byaldi! Thomas Keller of The French Laundry helped Pixar design the dish. [chuckles] True Disney nerd points if you got that one.

categories.title: Postcards from the Movies
categories.intro: Disney storytellers love a real-world road trip. [laughs] Name the real place that shows up in, or inspired, these films.

art.prompt: A vintage traveler's corkboard covered in blank illustrated postcards of a Gothic cathedral, a misty Hawaiian beach, a Bavarian castle on a cliff, and a pastel Italian fishing village, with string, pins, and a brass compass Original illustration, 16:9, rich saturated colors, cinematic lighting, no people, no characters, no text, no logos.

clues.clue: Quasimodo rings the bells high above Paris in this famous cathedral.
clues.reveal: [excited] The correct answer is Notre-Dame! The Hunchback of Notre Dame is set there, and the real cathedral reopened in 2024 after the big fire. [mischievously] Bells and all.

clues.clue: The Princess and the Frog is set in this jazzy U.S. city famous for beignets.
clues.reveal: [excited] The correct answer is New Orleans! And Disneyland's New Orleans Square serves Mickey-shaped beignets. Powdered sugar on your shirt is mandatory.

clues.clue: Lilo and Stitch live on this lush Hawaiian island, known as the Garden Isle.
clues.reveal: [excited] The correct answer is Kauai! The Garden Isle. Stitch would like to remind you that he is not a dog. He is a koala. [sarcastic] Allegedly.

clues.clue: This real Bavarian castle in Germany is often named as an inspiration for Sleeping Beauty Castle at Disneyland.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Neuschwanstein Castle! [laughs] Built by King Ludwig the Second, it's the fairy-tale castle fairy-tale castles want to be when they grow up.

clues.clue: Luca's seaside town of Portorosso is a love letter to this group of five Italian Riviera villages.
clues.reveal: [impressed] The correct answer is Cinque Terre! Director Enrico Casarosa grew up near there, and the Portorosso piazza borrows from the village of Vernazza. Silenzio, Bruno!

categories.title: Emoji Passport
categories.intro: [dramatic pause] Every one of these films is set somewhere you can sort of visit in World Showcase. I'll give you emoji and a hint. You give me the movie.

art.prompt: An open passport with rows of colorful blank stamp shapes floating up off the pages like glowing bubbles, a world globe and a paper airplane in the background, playful pop-art style Original illustration, 16:9, rich saturated colors, cinematic lighting, no people, no characters, no text, no logos.

clues.clue: Hint: a chilly musical about two royal sisters. ❄️👭⛄
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Frozen! Arendelle is inspired by Norway, and you can ride Frozen Ever After in EPCOT's Norway pavilion. [whispers] Let it go, let it go.

clues.clue: Hint: a family, a guitar, and a holiday in Mexico. 💀🎸🌼
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Coco! Those marigold petals guide the family home. [laughs] And if you said The Book of Life, nice try, but that one isn't even Disney.

clues.clue: Hint: a princess with a bow in the Scottish Highlands. 🏹🐻👑
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Brave! Merida shot for her own hand, and the closest World Showcase stop is the United Kingdom pavilion. Bring a bear-proof bag.

clues.clue: Hint: a warrior who takes her father's place, with a tiny dragon. 🗡️🐉🏯
clues.reveal: [dramatic pause] The correct answer is Mulan! The China pavilion is the perfect spot to strike a pose. Dishonor on anyone who missed this one. [chuckles] Dishonor on your cow!

clues.clue: Hint: a Pixar teen who poofs into an animal in Canada's biggest city. 🐼🔴🇨🇦
clues.reveal: [gasps] The correct answer is Turning Red! Mei poofs into a red panda in Toronto. Nobody tell her the Canada pavilion has lumberjacks. [mischievously] She'll get excited.

categories.title: Passport, Please
categories.intro: Time for a lap around World Showcase. I describe the spot, you name the pavilion's country. [chuckles] Comfortable shoes recommended.

art.prompt: A sunlit promenade around a lagoon lined with miniature country pavilions: a Norwegian stave church, a Moroccan gate with mosaic tiles, a red Japanese torii gate in the water, a German biergarten, a Mexican pyramid Original illustration, 16:9, rich saturated colors, cinematic lighting, no people, no characters, no text, no logos.

clues.clue: You can sail into Arendelle on the Frozen Ever After boat ride in this pavilion.
clues.reveal: [cheerful] The correct answer is Norway! Frozen Ever After replaced the old Maelstrom ride in 2016. Trolls, polar bears, and now a snowman who loves warm hugs.

clues.clue: This pavilion's centerpiece is a pyramid inspired by Mesoamerican temples, and the Three Caballeros ride boats inside it.
clues.reveal: [chuckles] The correct answer is Mexico! It's always twilight inside that pyramid, which is the perfect excuse for a margarita at any hour. [sarcastic] For the grown-ups.

clues.clue: A miniature Bavarian village with model trains chugging through it sits right next to this pavilion.
clues.reveal: [playfully] The correct answer is Germany! The little train village debuted at the 1995 Flower and Garden Festival and was supposed to be temporary. [laughs] Nobody let it leave.

clues.clue: King Hassan the Second sent skilled artisans to create the hand-cut tile mosaics in this pavilion, which opened in 1984.
clues.reveal: [impressed] The correct answer is Morocco! It was the first pavilion added after World Showcase opened. Those tiles were made by hand, so please don't lick them.

clues.clue: This pavilion's Mitsukoshi store is run by a retailer that traces its roots back to a kimono shop opened in 1673.
clues.reveal: [whispers] The correct answer is Japan! Mitsukoshi started as a kimono shop called Echigoya. Three hundred and fifty years of shopping, and I still can't find my wallet.

categories.title: Spaceship Earthlings
categories.intro: [excited] Our fans asked for EPCOT deep cuts, so here they are. Hope you remember the old days, or at least the big golf ball.

art.prompt: Interior of a futuristic 1980s-style pavilion glowing with purple and teal neon, a giant faceted silver sphere overhead, a fountain of leaping water arcs, retro-futurist monorail track sweeping past Original illustration, 16:9, rich saturated colors, cinematic lighting, no people, no characters, no text, no logos.

clues.clue: This giant geodesic sphere at the front of EPCOT is also a slow-moving dark ride.
clues.reveal: [excited] The correct answer is Spaceship Earth! Yes, the golf ball. Everybody calls it the golf ball. [laughs] Please don't try to tee off.

clues.clue: EPCOT Center first opened its gates in this year.
clues.reveal: [excited] The correct answer is 1982! October 1, 1982, exactly eleven years after Magic Kingdom opened. Happy birthday, EPCOT.

clues.clue: One little spark! This purple dragon-like creature is the star of Journey Into Imagination.
clues.reveal: [excited] The correct answer is Figment! Two tiny wings, eyes big and yellow, horns of a steer, what a lovable fellow. Spyro? [chuckles] Wrong company, buddy.

clues.clue: EPCOT began as an acronym. The E-P-C-O-T stands for this.
choices: Experimental Park of Culture and Technology
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Experimental Prototype Community of Tomorrow! [mischievously] Although Every Person Comes Out Tired is also technically accurate after a full day of World Showcase.

clues.clue: Figment's original bearded human companion, who flew a dream-catching machine on the 1983 version of Journey Into Imagination.
clues.reveal: [impressed] The correct answer is Dreamfinder! He left the ride in 1998, and EPCOT fans have been asking for him back ever since. We miss you, big red beard.
